clips.end_words: Ascorbic acid is not vitamin C
clips.send: A mom sends this to her sister who swears by her gummy vitamins - anger at realizing the "vitamin C" on the label may not act like vitamin C at all.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau told a story about scurvy on his show: sailors on long voyages got it, and real citrus (oranges, lemons, limes) made it go away every time, no exceptions.

His point: ascorbic acid, the "vitamin C" on most supplement labels, isn't the same thing. In nature, vitamin C never travels alone - it's bonded to bioflavonoids and other cofactors a lab-made version leaves out.

His test: give someone with scurvy pure ascorbic acid instead of real citrus, and it doesn't work the same way.

Next time you flip a label, does it just say "vitamin C," or does it actually name the source?

#kevintrudeau #vitaminc #supplementfacts #readthelabel #wholefood #healthtruth

clips.end_words: flushing money right down the toilet
clips.send: A friend sends this to someone who swallows a multivitamin every morning without a second thought - anxiety that their money (and the pill) is going straight through them.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau explained on his show why so many vitamin pills are coated in shellac, the same resin used on wood furniture.

It's there to help the pill survive the bottle, not to help your body absorb it. Chemical binders hold the pill's shape the same way glue does.

His simple test: drop one in a glass of water overnight. If it hasn't dissolved by morning, he says it likely didn't dissolve inside you either.

He tells of a family whose septic tank was packed with undigested pills after years of swallowing supplements whole.

Have you ever tried the glass-of-water test on your own vitamins?

#kevintrudeau #vitamins #supplementfacts #readthelabel #wholefood #healthtruth

clips.end_words: never buy anything from that company ever again
clips.send: A friend sends this to someone who takes a B-complex for energy - anger at discovering "niacin" on the label might be a renamed substitute.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau told a story on his show about a vitamin ingredient called niacin, and the harmless side effect some people don't like: a few minutes of flushed, hot skin.

Rather than keep selling real niacin, he says one company's chemists created a different substance, niacinamide, that skips the flush, then kept calling it niacin on the label.

His advice: check your own bottle. "Niacin (as niacinamide)" isn't the nutrient your body is asking for.

Why swap the real ingredient for one that just won't bother you?

#kevintrudeau #niacin #supplementfacts #readthelabel #wholefood #healthtruth
